html:
A lake north of Amsterdam that was pumped dry between 1609 and 1612 and laid out as farmland. It was one of the first large land reclamations of the Dutch Republic.

Merchants of Amsterdam put up the money, hoping to profit from new land. The engineer Jan Leeghwater helped build the dike around the lake and the rows of windmills that lifted the water out, step by step, into a ring canal. The first attempt was flooded when the dike broke, but the work was finished in 1612.

The new land was laid out on a strict grid of roads, ditches and square plots, an idea of order taken from Renaissance planning. Farms and country houses for the merchants followed. The Beemster was a model for later drainage across the Netherlands, and the old field pattern survives almost unchanged. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999.
sum: A lake north of Amsterdam that was pumped dry between 1609 and 1612 and laid out as farmland. It was one of the first large land reclamations of the Dutch Republic.
